subject.title: Browser: support blocked URL paths / domain denylist

question: Should OpenClaw add an enforceable browser navigation deny/warn policy, and what URL classes and browser traffic paths must it cover?
rationale: The request adds public security/config semantics that current browser SSRF hostname allowlists do not define, and automation should not choose whether this is hard egress control, advisory bot-block guidance, or part of a broader web egress policy.

options.title: Design Browser Policy Contract First
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define browser-specific block and warning semantics, then implement schema, guard, docs, and focused tests against that contract.

options.title: Fold Into Shared Egress Policy
options.body: Make the broader egress-firewall work own browser navigation too, but only after it explicitly covers browser redirects, subframes, proxy routing, and warnlist behavior.

options.title: Advisory Hints Only
options.body: Avoid an enforceable browser denylist and instead surface best-effort known bot-block warnings that do not claim to prevent network access.

recommendation.title: Design Browser Policy Contract First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define browser-specific block and warning semantics, then implement schema, guard, docs, and focused tests against that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The browser SSRF hardening and browser plugin policy history most strongly points to steipete for the security-boundary choice.
